Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Mozambique's Tax Authority indicated that after submitting e-declarations, taxpayers pay taxes using banking channels for payment of the respective tax, showing digital revenue collection capability.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Tax Authority's e-Declaracao/Portal do Contribuinte system (live since 2022 and still active in 2025) requires VAT, ISPC, IRPC and IRPS declarations electronically, with tax payment via banking channels (ATM, internet banking, mobile banking, POS); mandatory e-invoicing from May 2025 (DLA Piper, 2025) further evidences comprehensive digital revenue collection. Value Code 3 (Yes) confirmed.

Comments: G2P via SIMOrede is described as a planned "next development phase" (social disbursements) rather than already active at national scale; evidence indicates preparation but not full active use on the IPS.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at Limited Use, but flagged for human review. AfricaNenda (Nov 2025) states G2P specifically on the SIMOrede IPS is the 'next development phase', not yet live. However, a separate government channel (SPA/e-SISTAFE) has disbursed social payments digitally at meaningful scale: over 200,000 beneficiaries by March 2023 (World Bank) and 208,708 electronic payments in the 2025 PASP cycle (360Mozambique, March 2026). Whether this counts as 'the instant payment system' for this indicator is ambiguous and should be resolved by a human reviewer; the code is left unchanged pending that decision.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: Bank of Mozambique (BoM) is deeply involved: it holds the majority of shares in SIMO and appoints the chairperson of SIMO's board; it is also the settlement agent and BoM approves fees/pricing for the IPS.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strengthened. AfricaNenda (Nov 2025) confirms the Bank of Mozambique is majority shareholder of SIMO, appoints the board chairperson, approves fees, and acts as settlement agent; Notice No. 1/GBM/2026 (25 February 2026, in force 2 March 2026, per DLA Piper) shows BoM formally creating and regulating the national instant payment system (SPIM), operated by SIMO. Value Code 4 (Board Representation) confirmed, since SIMO (not BoM directly) remains the operator.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: SIMOrede includes dispute resolution governed by IPS scheme rules and SIMO has a dedicated dispute/complaints team, indicating some consumer-protection mechanisms, but public legal framework specific to payments was not found in accessible sources during this pass.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised up to Yes. Banco de Mocambique's Aviso n.2/GBM/2014 (read via Boletim da Republica, 2014) is a dedicated regulation on the provision of electronic payment products/services, requiring pre-disclosure of terms and conditions and allocating liability to the credit institution/payment provider (Article 7), with exceptions for proven customer negligence. This is supplemented by Aviso n.9/GBM/2020 (complaints-handling regulation, 30-day response requirement) and the broader Aviso n.8/GBM/2021 financial consumer protection code. Together these are specific, published, payment-relevant regulations rather than only general or partial provisions.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: SIMO shares daily transactions reports with participants for reconciliation and provides consolidated transaction files to BoM for settlement, but this is not described as public reporting; however, AfricaNenda provides annual-type performance statistics (e.g., transaction volumes 2020-2024), suggesting at least ad hoc public performance disclosure via reports.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised up to Monthly/Quarterly. Banco de Mocambique's own statistics portal publishes 'Compensacao Electronica' bulletins under 'Estatisticas do Sistema Nacional de Pagamentos' on an explicitly stated monthly schedule (e.g., the September 2023 bulletin page states 'Frequencia de Publicacao: Mensal' with fixed publication and next-publication dates). This is regular, public, official reporting by the regulator, going well beyond the ad hoc participant-level reconciliation described in the original source, so the code is revised upward.

Comments: AfricaNenda notes SIMO "has yet to implement a pro-poor governance structure"; only banks are represented on the board and thus it has not achieved progressed inclusivity (i.e., limited pro-poor governance mechanisms).

This is a clear statement of absence rather than a partial mechanism, so the evidence supports No rather than Partial.
